summary_paraphrase: Left alone in the bath for a few moments, a boy turns sponges, the tap and bubbles into a safari of crocodile, elephant, giraffe and hippo until a lion roars; his mother comes back, bathtime ends, and he falls asleep among toy versions of the animals.

beats.function: sound, unfinished line, new animal: repeated cycle

characters.name: Jack
characters.change: from bath to imagined safari and back to bed; no inner change

characters.name: Mom
characters.personality: cheerful; frames the play by leaving and returning
characters.humor_source: may have been the roarer (picture only)

characters.name: lion
characters.relation_to_protagonist: the one threat; never meets Jack on the page

humor_notes: Visual and sound-driven: bath objects become animals, the rest-sigh drawn with sunglasses, a giraffe neck used as a slide; the roar may be Mom (picture only).

repetition.description: each animal arrives the same way: a sound word, a half line that stops mid-sentence, then the animal on the next spread
repetition.why: the unfinished lines invite the listener to guess before the turn, and the picture always answers

repetition.description: bath objects from page 1 (sponges, bottles, tap) return as animals, and all animals return as toys around the bed
repetition.why: the toys at bedtime close the fantasy and land it safely at home

notes: No animal is named in the text; every animal is identified only by the picture (and one by its trumpet).
Every bath object (sponge, tap, bottles) is drawn becoming its animal, so the picture carries the logic of the imagined game.
The 'aaah' line is a rest sigh in the picture, not a scream: the picture reverses how a listener would hear the word.
The last story page is wordless: sleep and the toy animals close the book without text.

strengths: five spreads end on a half line the picture completes after the turn
picture carries all the animals, so the words stay very few
wordless sleeping page as a closing ritual
weaknesses: almost meaningless without pictures: as text alone it is a list of sounds
no problem or inner change; the lion threat is dropped rather than resolved
premise of a young child alone in the bath

anti_patterns.note: the lion threat is raised and then dropped when Mom returns; nothing is at stake for Jack

child_appeal_heuristic.label: Research heuristic — not validated
child_appeal_heuristic.rationale: Scores are the analyst's reading of the pages, not observations of children.

age_suitability.notes: A young child is left alone in the bath and plays roughly in the water; as a model keep the imagined-play frame and the bedtime landing, drop the unattended bath. The lion roar is research intensity 4 of 5 for one page, about 2 on the engine's 0-3 scale, defused on the next spread. Text alone does not tell the story (MagicPaper stories are text-only today).

metrics.lexicon_note: direct_address and sound_words are lexicon counts: a floor, not a measure. direct_address counts second-person words anywhere, dialogue included — it is not narrator-to-reader address

repetition.end_rhyme_note: heuristic: consecutive lines sharing a final two letters
